title: Where the money goes: token economics
summary: A model bill is the sum of uncached input, cached input, cache writes, output and reasoning tokens, multiplied by the number of calls a task makes. Knowing which sink dominates tells you which lever to pull.
useIf: The bill grew faster than traffic, or you must price a new feature before you build it.
avoidIf: You treat it as a one-number exercise: cost per token alone hides retries, loops and failed tasks.

explain.md: Every request pays for several token categories. **Uncached input** is full price. **Cached input** is a read of reused prefix state: 0.1x the uncached rate on OpenAI GPT-5.6 and later, and 0.05x on GPT-6.1 Sol [[r25]]. A **cache write** costs 1.25x on those models, and OpenAI bills each token at exactly one of the uncached, cached or write rates. One write plus nine reads costs 2.15x against 10x uncached [[r25]]. Anthropic charges 1.25x for a 5-minute write, 2x for a 1-hour write and 0.1x for a read [[r26]]. **Output** tokens come last, and **reasoning tokens** sit inside the completion count, so a short visible answer can hide a long generation [[r27]].

The visible prompt is rarely the biggest sink. **Tool definitions**, the **system prompt** and the **history** are re-sent on every call. An **agent loop** multiplies all of it by the number of model calls per task. With a constant 500 new tokens per turn, 20 turns process 500 x (1 + 2 + ... + 20) = 105,000 input tokens for 10,000 tokens of new content (derived). Caching and compaction exist to flatten that curve.

explain.title: Where tokens go in one agent step
explain.alt: Tool definitions, system prompt, history and retrieved context form the prompt. The model call returns reasoning and answer tokens, and the next step re-sends the grown prompt.
explain.src:
flowchart LR
  T[Tool definitions] --> P[Prompt]
  S[System prompt] --> P
  H[History] --> P
  C[Retrieved context] --> P
  P --> M[Model call]
  M --> R[Reasoning tokens]
  M --> A[Answer tokens]
  A --> H

explain.title: Cost per successful task
explain.expr: cost per task = sum over calls (uncached x p_in + cached x 0.1 x p_in + written x 1.25 x p_in + output x p_out) / task success rate

vars.v: your price sheet per input and output token (not quoted here, prices change)
read and write multipliers on GPT-5.6 and later [[r25]]
share of tasks that finish correctly; retries and failures raise cost per task

explain.example: Five requests share one prefix inside its lifetime. Cost in units of one uncached prefix: 1.25 + 4 x 0.1 = 1.65, against 5.0 uncached (derived).

whereToUse: A finance review of a bill that grew faster than traffic
Pricing a new assistant or agent feature before launch
Choosing the first cost lever: batch, cache, trim, route or limit output
Per-tenant or per-team chargeback, using gateway token metrics [[r3]]
Comparing two models by cost per successful task, not price per million tokens

use: Spend is rising and nobody can say which consumer or prompt section drives it
You are about to switch models or add caching and need a baseline
Agents or tools make several model calls per user task
You need chargeback by team, tenant or feature
avoid: You treat it as a one-number exercise: cost per token alone hides retries, loops and failed tasks
Optimising a workload whose monthly spend is small against engineering time
Cutting tokens on a path where quality is not yet measured
flips: Reasoning-heavy workload: output and reasoning tokens dominate, so measure completion tokens first
Long static prefix with high reuse: cached reads dominate and the write premium matters
Mostly asynchronous work: batch pricing changes the baseline by half

pitfalls.symptom: The bill doubled while traffic grew 20%
pitfalls.cause: Longer prompts, growing history, more agent steps or a switch to a reasoning model, not more users
pitfalls.fix: Attribute tokens by consumer and by prompt section, then compare tokens per task before and after

pitfalls.symptom: Caching was enabled and cost went up
pitfalls.cause: On GPT-5.6 and later a write costs 1.25x, so a prefix used once loses 25% [[r25]]
pitfalls.fix: Cache only prefixes reused at least twice inside the lifetime, or use explicit mode with no breakpoints

pitfalls.symptom: A cheaper model raised cost per task
pitfalls.cause: More retries, longer outputs or extra agent steps offset the lower price
pitfalls.fix: Track cost per successful task and tokens per task, not price per token

scenarios.title: The bill doubled, traffic did not
scenarios.situation: A support assistant answers questions with retrieval. Monthly model spend doubled while requests grew 20%. Nobody owns the prompt, and several teams call one shared deployment.
constraints: Prices and model mix are unknown
One shared deployment serves several teams
unknowns: Did the average prompt or the average output grow?
Which team or feature grew fastest?
Did anyone change the model, effort level or retrieval depth?
scenarios.question: What do you do first?

options.name: Attribute tokens by consumer and prompt section, then pick the biggest sink
options.why: Without attribution any lever is a guess. A gateway metric by team and a split of prompt tokens into system, tools, history and retrieval show where growth came from.
options.tradeoff: Costs a day or two of instrumentation before any saving lands.

options.name: Swap to the cheapest model for every request
options.why: It cuts price per token but may raise retries, output length and escalations, and it changes quality unmeasured.
options.tradeoff: Right only after evals show the cheap model passes the quality bar on this task mix.

options.name: Lower max_tokens everywhere
options.why: Output is the costliest token class and caps are cheap to ship.
options.tradeoff: Truncated answers hurt quality if the cap is below natural answer length; it does not touch input growth.

flips.if: Attribution shows 70% of tokens are an unchanged 9,000-token prefix
flips.then: Fix prefix ordering and caching first.

flips.if: One batch-like consumer grew fastest and nobody waits for it
flips.then: Move that consumer to Batch for half price.

scenarios.takeaway: Attribute first. The lever follows the sink.

scenarios.title: A cheap-looking classifier
scenarios.situation: A classification endpoint runs 5 million short requests a day on a reasoning model. Visible answers are one word. Cost is far above the estimate from the price sheet.
unknowns: How many reasoning tokens does each call use?
What accuracy does a non-reasoning model reach on the labelled set?
scenarios.question: Where is the money going and what is the fix?

options.name: Check completion token details for reasoning tokens, then lower effort or use a non-reasoning model if evals hold
options.why: Reasoning tokens count inside completion tokens, so a one-word answer can cost thousands of hidden tokens.
options.tradeoff: Accuracy must be re-measured on the labelled set before the switch.

options.name: Add a semantic cache
options.why: Repeated short inputs can hit, saving whole calls.
options.tradeoff: Adds an embedding and lookup per miss, and wrong hits are a quality risk.

options.name: Buy PTUs for the volume
options.why: It changes how you pay, not how many tokens each call burns.
options.tradeoff: Right after tokens per call are minimised and traffic is steady.

flips.then: Batch the work for half price.
Keep reasoning on hard cases only, behind a router.

scenarios.takeaway: Hidden reasoning tokens turn a one-word answer into a large bill.

quiz.q: A prefix is written once at 1.25x and then read 4 more times at 0.1x inside its lifetime. What is the total cost, in units of one uncached pass over the prefix?
quiz.explain: 1.25 + 4 x 0.1 = 1.65. Five uncached passes would cost 5.0. The same arithmetic on one write plus nine reads gives the 2.15x in the OpenAI guide [[r25]].

quiz.q: A user sends one message and the agent makes 10 model calls. Which of these are paid as input tokens on each of the 10 calls?
options: Earlier tool results kept in history
quiz.explain: Tool definitions, the system prompt and the accumulated history are re-sent every call. The user message is not the only input; it is one small part. Caching lowers the price of the repeated parts but does not remove them.

quiz.q: Cost per token fell 40% after a model switch, but cost per task rose. Which cause is most consistent?
options: The new model needs more steps and retries per task
quiz.explain: More steps and longer outputs raise tokens per task faster than price per token fell. Cached reads and batch pricing both lower cost, so neither explains a rise.

flashcards.front: On GPT-5.6 and later, what do cache writes and reads cost relative to uncached input?
flashcards.back: Write 1.25x, read 0.1x (0.05x on GPT-6.1 Sol). One write plus nine reads is 2.15x against 10x uncached.

flashcards.front: Why can a one-word answer be expensive?
flashcards.back: Reasoning tokens count inside completion tokens. The hidden generation is billed even when the visible answer is short.

flashcards.front: Which metric hides retries and agent loops?
flashcards.back: Cost per token. Track cost per successful task and tokens per task instead.
